events.name: valence_salience_listener
events.hypothesis: Listeners interpret referring expressions through the speaker's evaluative stance, modulating their prior expectations about object salience by the speaker's valence. When a speaker describes their favorite object, listeners expect them to favor feature-rich referents, whereas when describing a least favorite object, that preference shifts toward simpler, feature-poor objects.

events.name: feature_rarity_prior
events.hypothesis: People's prior expectations over referents are governed by contextual feature rarity: an object is salient to the extent that its features are rare and informative within the visual scene, with features shared across fewer competitors contributing more strongly to salience. On the complex reference display where two objects have equal feature counts but one possesses a uniquely distinguishing feature, the current shared-prior model assigns them equal prior probability and predicts listeners choose the shared-feature object, whereas the contextual rarity mechanism predicts listeners choose the unique-feature competitor instead.

events.name: silent_alternative_speaker

The pragmatic listener reasons about this communicative choice, inferring that a speaker who chose to speak rather than remain silent possessed a strong communicative reason to do so. On prior trials without an informative word, the listener chooses uniformly across objects.

live.name: contextual_contrast_prior
